subject: Traffic-to-commit gateways and forecasted thresholds
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Elliot Ramos <elliot.ramos@cobaltai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Grace Oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Traffic-to-commit gateways and forecasted thresholds

Elliot —

Thanks again for the time this morning. I pulled the Q2 usage slices and a short latency/ROI snapshot to help frame the renewal conversation. Attached: CSV with monthly token breakdown by route, and our latency bench PDF showing 95th / p50 splits across your primary models. Quick summary up front:

- Current run-rate: ~1.8B tokens/mo (50% embeddings, 50% text gen).
- Peak burst window: 2.7B tokens in a 24-hour period (early-Aug deploy).
- Latency: p95 for the chat route rose from 320ms -> 420ms during the peak; this is where caching and routing could help most.

Suggested next steps for a pragmatic renewal that preserves performance while hedging spend:
1) Gate: Introduce a two-tranche commit (Base + Headroom). Base = 2B tokens/mo (annual), Headroom = incremental monthly block billed at a discounted token rate until monthly usage exceeds headroom for 90 days.
2) SLA smoothing: Keep current p95 SLA but add a burst-credit allowance for seasonal spikes (we propose 10% burst credit per quarter).
3) Operational play: We’ll implement prefix caching for high-frequency queries and route lower-priority batch traffic to a quantized-serving tier. Estimated cost delta: ~8–12% reduction in per-token spend for text-gen on the pilot routes.

Ben and Grace — attaching the detailed CSV and latency PDF. Can you confirm the typical routes you want included in the Headroom gating? Elliot — if procurement wants the term amendment in advance I can push a draft (DocuSign) once we align on numbers.

Regards,
Mina
Mina Haddad
Senior Renewal Lead, Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.com

Attachments (stubs): redwood_q2_usage_breakdown.csv (csv), latency_benchmarks_Q2.pdf (pdf)
From: Elliot Ramos <elliot.ramos@cobaltai.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@cobaltai.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 11:04:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Traffic-to-commit gateways and forecasted thresholds

Thanks Mina — this is helpful and aligns with what we saw internally. A few clarifications from our side:

- The 2.7B burst on Aug 8 was driven by a batch re-index job; that route is low-priority and can be scheduled off-peak.
- The chat p95 impact is customer-facing; we want to avoid any noticeable regressions.
- Our finance lead asks for at least one contractual month of lookback flexibility in H1 of any annual commit so we don't overpay for a temporary growth blip.

Request: can you separate the CSV into 'customer-facing' vs 'background' routes and push an updated estimate on cost delta that assumes background traffic is compressed into off-peak lanes? If it helps, Ben — happy to set a short call tomorrow with our infra PM to walk traffic labels.

— Elliot
Elliot Ramos
Head of Platform, Cobalt AI
elliot.ramos@cobaltai.com
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Elliot Ramos <elliot.ramos@cobaltai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Grace Oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, procurement@cobaltai.com
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 08:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Traffic-to-commit gateways and forecasted thresholds

Elliot — thanks, great context. I split the routes and re-ran the numbers. Attached: updated CSV with two tabs (customer-facing / background) and a one-page ROI summary embedded in the sheet. Key takeaways:

- If background traffic is scheduled to off-peak lanes and routed to a quantized tier, estimated annual spend delta: -11% on total platform cost (assuming current mix).
- Keeping 2B tokens/mo as Base covers current steady-state; headroom tier of 800M tokens/mo covers most short spikes and keeps the per-token rate within the committed tier until we hit sustained growth (90-day rule).
- Proposal for lookback flexibility: allow one lookback month per 12-month rolling period to be counted against future headroom reconciliations (this addresses procurement's risk without rewriting the commit economics).

I also translated these into two contract options (summary in the attached amendment_term_sheet_v1.pdf):
A) Conservative: 2B Base / 800M Headroom, 10% quarterly burst credit, standard SLA.
B) Growth-friendly: 2.5B Base / 500M Headroom, smaller per-token discount but higher guaranteed capacity (useful if you lock in model pinning for peak routes).

If Cobalt signs Option A, we’ll prepare a DocuSign amendment and include a 60-day pilot period for the caching/quantization changes so CS can validate p95 improvements.

Action items:
- Elliot: confirm which option (A/B) you prefer or flag modifications.
- Procurement: confirm the lookback language is acceptable — happy to add legal-friendly wording before signature.
- Ben/Grace: queue the pilot (1–2 weeks) and propose start date windows.

I’ve attached the amendment draft and the revised usage sheet.

Thanks,
Mina

Attachments (stubs): amendment_term_sheet_v1.pdf (pdf), redwood_q2_usage_breakdown_split.csv (csv)

Procurement — when you have a moment, I’ll send the DocuSign link for Option A with the lookback language baked into Section 4.3.

Next steps:

- DocuSign to procurement on sign-off path.
